content:
alex: FYI ran extended throughput sweep for Qwen-14B + Mixtral-8B variants using the new paged-slab KV layout. Observed a ~18% throughput drop when slab coalescing is enabled on Qwen. Suspect RoPE scaling or head/dim mismatch interacting with kernel selection.

jin: ugh. can you paste the run command and the profiler snapshot?

alex: sure — command: `./bench --model qwen-14b --kv-layout=paged-slab --slab-coalesce=1 --num_key_value_heads=64 --kv-dim=128 --batching=continuous`

alex: profiler top lines (summarized):
```
kernel_dispatch: +42% (matmul_fwd_small)
kv_paged_read: +33%
kv_coalesce_merge: +21%
rope_apply_scale: +15%
batch_assembler_wait: -8%
```

maria: interesting that matmul_fwd_small jumps. could be kernel chooser preferring a suboptimal small-kernel path once slabs are merged. Coalescing changes sequence lengths to the kernel selector heuristics.

sara: do we have head/dim mismatches between model config and runtime? e.g., num_key_value_heads vs actual attention heads per layer. If those diverge, KV packing layout changes and can fragment pages.

devon: i also noticed latency p50 increases slightly and p99 spikes with slabs on. throughput drop but burst latency worse -> paging thrash maybe.

alex: attached more logs (excerpt):
`KV pages allocated: 2458 -> after coalesce: 818`
`avg page occupancy: 0.31 -> 0.77`
`page_frags_detected: 72`

jin: page count went down but fragmentation detected increased — suggests coalescing merged sparse fragments but left some large holes that make kernel memory access patterns worse.

maria: quick experiment suggestion: run with `--num_key_value_heads=32` and `--kv-dim=256` to keep per-head dim similar to Mixtral shapes; try toggling `RUNTIME_KERNEL_PREFERENCE=throughput_vs_latency` to force different kernel selection.

alex: queued runs: 1) slab off, 2) slab on + force kernel preference=latency, 3) slab on + num_kv_heads=32, 4) slab on + kv_dim=256. starting now.

perf-bot: automated note: CI bench job #1253 started on builder-7 (qwen-14b slab-coalesce sweep). Link: https://ci.redwood/bench/1253

sara: while experiments run, can we profile `rope_apply_scale` deeper? If RoPE scaling factor changes kernel tiling (we saw tile size bump from 128 -> 192 on Qwen layer 10) then matmuls could fall off fast-path.

devon: also check `kv_page_compact_threshold` — default is 0.6, maybe coalescing raises occupancy but leaves some pages under threshold causing extra metadata scanning.

jin: run 2 done: forcing latency-preferred kernels recovered ~10% of throughput but still ~9% below baseline (no coalesce). p99 improved.

alex: run 3 done: setting `--num_key_value_heads=32` reclaimed almost all throughput (now within 2% of baseline). suspects: our qwen runtime assumed 64 kv heads for packing; coalescing changed layout leading to misaligned per-head stride.

maria: that matches a hypothesis: when num_kv_heads changed, the kernel selection logic selects a different matmul tile because inner-dim mod changes. Kernel tables need to account for coalesced page packing shapes.

alex: run 4 (kv_dim=256) gave marginal improvement but increased memory working set -> more occasional OOMs on smaller nodes. Not ideal.

devon: next steps: 1) add a kernel chooser check that considers `kv_layout==paged-slab && slab_coalesce==1` as a separate shape family, 2) add a warning when runtime-configured `num_key_value_heads` != model's nominal kv heads, 3) conservative default: disable slab coalescing for Qwen-like head layouts until kernel table update shipped.

maria: +1. also add a small microkernel test in our CI: pack a synthetic KV page shape (coalesced occupancy patterns) and run matmul bench to validate that chosen kernel is optimal.

alex: filing follow-ups: GH issues created: #infra-kernel-chooser (kernel family for paged-slab-coalesce), #runtime-config-check (warn on kv head mismatch), #ci-microbench (kv-page synthetic shapes).

perf-bot: created issues: https://gh.redwood/infra-kernel-chooser, https://gh.redwood/runtime-config-check, https://gh.redwood/ci-microbench

jin: can someone write a short note for release notes: `fix: avoid performance regression for coalesced paged KV on Qwen models by validating kv-heads and improving kernel selection` — we'll gate until validated.

alex: will draft a short blurb. thanks all, reassigning to devon to own the kernel-chooser PR. :thumbsup:
